title: Decoding the chromatin proteome of a single genomic locus by DNA sequencing
boundary: Pooled yeast clones pair a genomic locus barcode with an endogenous TAP-tagged protein. Tag-ChIP recovers each protein-associated barcode; separate input and ChIP barcode amplicons are sequenced and compared. This locus-proteome DNA reporter preparation differs from generic genome-wide ChIP-seq and from antibody-tag reporters. Multiple loci, proteins and perturbations remain one method.

title: Chem-map profiles drug binding to chromatin in cells
boundary: Biotinylated small molecule/anti-biotin complexes bind targets in permeabilized cells. A secondary-antibody/pA-Tn5 assembly marks nearby DNA by tagmentation, then extracted adapter-ended fragments undergo PCR/NGS. This chemical-affinity recruitment frontend differs from ordinary protein-directed CUT&Tag and from Chem-seq ligand-affinity capture of chromatin. Different drugs/targets are not extra methods; scEpiChem not added as an application/scale variant in this pass.

title: Genome-wide localization of small molecules
boundary: Chemical ligand-affinity capture recovers associated genomic chromatin for massively parallel DNA sequencing, with intact-cell and lysate routes within one method.
